details:
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Submission

What is this?

When we started thinking about how to get kids aged 7 to 12 interested in space exploration, we realized something: textbooks don't cut it. Space isn't just about cool rockets; it's about hard choices, limited resources, and problem-solving under pressure.

 

That’s why we built Junior Astrounaut; Mars Mission—a lightweight, browser-based simulation game where players step into the boots of a Junior Commander running a Martian base.

How it Works (The Core Gameplay)

Over the course of 3 Martian days (Sols), players have to keep their base alive by balancing three critical resources:

  •  Energy: For heating and power grids.

 

  • Oxygen: For life support.

 

  • Shielding: To protect the crew from cosmic hazards.

 

Every turn throws a real scenario at the player (like a sudden solar radiation spike or a dust storm), forcing them to make a tough trade-off. There is no "perfect" choice, just like real space missions—every decision has a cost.

Grounded in Real NASA Data

We wanted this game to be scientifically honest, not just sci-fi fiction.

  • We pulled real concepts from NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database) to shape our solar storm events.

 

  • We looked at NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository) principles for life-support and bioreactor efficiency.

 

Whenever players make a choice, brief educational pop-ups explain the real science behind what just happened, so kids learn by doing.

Built for Accessibility

We built this using the Godot Engine (Compatibility Renderer) and exported it straight to HTML5. Why? Because the best educational games are the ones you can play instantly. No heavy downloads, no installation steps—just click the link on itch.io and play right inside your browser.

 

Try it out, manage your resources carefully, and see if your crew can survive 3 Sols on Mars!
